extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, researchers, patent office statisticians, and IP analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and metrics for constructing, reporting and interpreting patent statistics (filings, grants, families, PCT activity, processing, opposition, cost and intensity indicators) for comparative and policy analysis. Includes definitions, data-source practices, counting conventions and caveats for cross-country and temporal comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is an exclusive right granted by law to applicants/assignees to make use of and exploit their inventions for a limited period of time (generally 20 years from filing); in return the applicant must disclose the invention to the public in a manner that enables others skilled in the art to replicate the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the policy balance between exclusive rights and disclosure; background concept used to motivate why patent statistics indicate inventive activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent statistics as an indicator of inventive activity (caveats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent statistics are a reliable (although not perfect) indicator of innovative activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to consider when using patent statistics: not all inventions are patented (alternatives like trade secrecy); use of patent system varies across countries and industries; different filing strategies and filing preferences complicate direct comparisons; differences in national patent systems influence filing decisions; R&D and protection may occur in different locations; cross-border filings depend on trade flows, FDI, market size, etc. 'Notwithstanding the points mentioned above, patent statistics do provide valuable information about innovative activity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Date conventions for indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent indicators are constructed according to specific date concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists used conventions: patent filing (application) indicators are based on the patent filing date; patent grant indicators are based on the grant date; patent families data are based on the priority (first filing) date; technology indicators are based on the publication date. Use the appropriate date depending on the indicator being measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country of origin (counting rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Country of origin is based on the country of residence of the first-named applicant (or assignee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes country of residence of inventor vs applicant: inventor residence may indicate location of invention, applicant residence indicates owner at time of application. Notes inclusion of companies domiciled in a country but effectively owned/controlled by overseas interests; resident vs non-resident filings definitions are given (resident filing = application filed at office of State where first-named applicant has residence; non-resident filing = filed where first-named applicant does not have residence). Use the first-named applicant rule for country-of-origin statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident versus non-resident filings/grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident filing refers to an application filed at an office of the State in which the first-named applicant has residence; non-resident filing refers to an application filed where the first-named applicant does not have residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report distributions of resident and non-resident shares (e.g., rising share of non-resident filings over time). Use these categories for office-level and country-level analysis; be aware of large differences across offices (some offices >90% non-resident filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total patent filings (aggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of patent applications filed across offices (global filing counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report total filings and growth rates (e.g., estimated 1.76 million in 2006; mean yearly growth rates). Present both aggregate totals and trends (year-on-year growth). Note differences between filings and other economic indicators when interpreting growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent filings by patent office
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent filings broken down by filing office (e.g., USPTO, JPO, SIPO, KIPO, EPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide long-term trends by office and top-office rankings for a given year. Also show distribution of resident vs non-resident filings at each office and note office-specific routing peculiarities (e.g., EPO regional route vs national).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent filings by country of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent filings by the country of residence of the first-named applicant (top origins, shares).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report country shares, top origin rankings, and changes over time (e.g., share changes for Japan, China, U.S.). Include the note that data include filings in home office as well as filings abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent families (definition and use)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent family is defined as a set of patent applications inter-related by either priority claims or PCT national phase entries, normally containing the same subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use patent-family based statistics to eliminate double counting of the same invention filed across multiple offices. Patent families are based on priority/first filing date and useful for measuring unique inventions and internationalization of filing activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family size distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of patent family size measured by number of offices in which applications for the same invention are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report shares of families filed in 1, 2, 3, 4 or more offices; use this to infer internationalization (e.g., % families filed in ≥2 offices, ≥4 offices). Note large variation by origin country (some origins produce mostly domestic-oriented families).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent families by origin and destination (origin–destination breakdown)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of patent families by country/owner of origin and destination offices included in the family (which offices applicants choose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for indicating ownership of invention and regional protection strategies (e.g., share of families from certain origins including USPTO, EPO, SIPO, JPO, KIPO). Present per-origin destination mixes and discuss geographic/market influences (proximity, market size).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total patent grants (aggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total patents granted across patent offices (global grant counts and growth rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report total grants, growth volatility, and cross-year comparisons. Note grants depend on office resources (examiners, IT) and can be more volatile than filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grants by office and by country of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patents granted broken down by granting office and by country of origin of applicant/owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide office-level trends, top granting offices, distribution of resident vs non-resident grants. Note regional differences and parallel routes affecting grant counts (e.g., EPO vs national).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force (stock) and age profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patents currently in force and their age distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report total patents in force by office and by country of origin and provide age-profile (e.g., many patents in force were filed in a recent multi-year window). Note that relatively few patents are maintained for the full 20-year term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility models (definition and metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model: special form of IP rights for inventions granted for a fixed (shorter) time period with different terms/less stringent examination than normal patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report utility model filings and grants where available as an alternative to patents; note terminological differences across countries and that availability of utility models affects standard patent counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: International filings via the PCT (counts and interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counting of international applications filed through the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) and national-phase entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report PCT international phase filings and PCT national phase entries; clarify that PCT applications are not 'international patents' and that granting remains with national/regional offices. Note incomplete national-phase data prior to certain years and that some EPC member states close their national-phase route (require entering regional EPO phase instead). Use receiving-office and designated/elected-office breakdowns and by country of origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT filings by ownership type and filing route
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT filings broken down by applicant ownership type and by filing route used (national, regional, PCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PCT filings by applicant ownership categories and analyze non-resident filings by filing route. Use to indicate internationalization and how different jurisdictions are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent activity by field of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent filings and foreign-oriented patent families classified by field of technology (IPC concordance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use publication-date-based technology indicators and provide breakdowns by technology fields (e.g., computer tech, telecommunications, electrical machinery, energy technologies). Use concordance tables (IPC and technologies) to map classification to technology sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Specialization Index (RSI) of foreign-oriented patent families
rubrics_metrics.description: An index measuring specialization of origins in foreign-oriented patent families by technology or destination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RSI to identify relative specialization patterns across origins and technology fields (Annex provides RSI tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent intensity indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of patenting intensity such as resident patent filings per GDP, per million population, and per R&D expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute resident filings per billion US$ GDP, per million population, per million US$ R&D (R&D lagged by 2 years as used here). Provide trends to compare patenting intensity across countries controlling for economic size and R&D inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent processing activity metrics (pendency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics describing patent office processing workload such as pendency volume and time, number of pending applications, months to first office action and total pendency time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report pending application counts, trends, and time-to-first-action and total pendency; explain procedural causes (e.g., shortening request-for-examination periods increases short-term backlog). Use to highlight capacity challenges and backlog trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and invalidation statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics on numbers of opposition and invalidation requests received by patent offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report opposition/invalidation counts by office and correlate with grants; analyze trends and note that increased numbers may reflect greater third-party interest in challenging patents. Be aware of exceptions (e.g., Germany decoupling trends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of patenting (metrics and methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-of-patenting indicators and the methodological approach to compute them (see Annex D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide components of cost (filing, prosecution, translation, national phase fees, renewals, attorney fees, etc.), assumptions used, and country/route-specific calculations. Include an annex/methodology and caution about comparability and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and compilation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary data sources: WIPO Statistics Database (annual office surveys and PCT data), PATSTAT for technology and family construction, World Bank and UNESCO for macroeconomic and R&D data; supplemental Trilateral and national office reports for pendency/opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document data provenance, coverage limitations, and supplements. State that missing data are estimated by WIPO when necessary and feasible, and that continual updating can change historical figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing, estimated and revised data
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy for estimating missing data and revising historical statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that missing data are estimated at aggregate levels when necessary; due to continual updating of missing data and revision of historical statistics, figures in this report may differ from previously published figures. Flag estimates in tables and text.

rubrics_metrics.name: National and regional patent system differences affecting statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in legal and procedural frameworks across national/regional patent systems that affect statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: availability of alternative forms of rights (utility models, provisional patents, design patents) that reduce standard patent counts; differences in patentable subject matter across jurisdictions (e.g., business methods); variation in automatic vs request-based search/examination procedures. Advise users to consult collected information on national system characteristics when interpreting indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting notes and coverage limitations (PCT specifics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific counting and coverage notes such as incomplete PCT national phase data prior to 1995 and closed national-phase routes for some EPC states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide caveats in tables (e.g., Note: PCT national phase entry data is incomplete prior to 1995). Explain how European PCT national-phase closure affects national office counts and why some national offices show lower-than-expected PCT entries (EPO regional phase entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary definitions used for consistent reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized glossary entries (e.g., resident filing, utility model, R&D expenditure) to ensure consistent interpretation of indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include glossary definitions and specify units (e.g., R&D expenditure in millions of constant US$ PPP, filings per million population). Use glossary terms when documenting tables and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex outputs and recommended tabulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard annexes and tables to include alongside headline indicators (Top PCT applicants, IPC–technology concordance, RSI tables, cost methodology, full statistical tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide recommended annex content and formats to allow replication and deeper analysis (e.g., Top PCT applicants list, IPC concordance, full office-by-origin tables).
